text:
Elaine: quick heads-up — started bring-up for ember-7b-quant with an 'approximate decode' pass (early experiments). 1.8x decode throughput on our 80-token median, but some quality wobble on commit tests. looking for quick eyeballs and eval plan suggestions.

Dmitri: nice. can you paste the perf numbers and quant config?

Elaine: perf snapshot (local dev rig, A100-80GB, batch=8):
```
model: ember-7b-quant
quant: q4_k_m (per-channel)
decode: approx-early-exit (heuristic confidence gate)
median latency/token: 9.2ms -> 5.1ms (approx)
throughput (tokens/sec): 1100 -> 2000
quality (MMLU acc): 62.1% -> 60.3%
```

Ben: 1.8x is great but 1.8 pts drop on MMLU is not great. how noisy are those evals? sample size?

Elaine: small sample (n=200 prompts) — that's just the quick pass. also saw some hallucination spike in the RAG regression set.

Sophia: propose a two-track eval: (1) wide holdout benchmark (MMLU, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA subsets, and our CustomerQA set) with n>=2000; (2) targeted prompt families where approx rules trigger (repetitive prefixes / short answers). we should measure both macro-accuracy and regression rate (fraction of prompts that change from correct->incorrect).

Dmitri: agree. also want a calibrated A/B flip test where we shadow-run exact decode on 10% of approx requests and compare token-level divergence and final answer delta. that isolates when the gate triggers poorly.

Elaine: good. quick note on the heuristic: uses top-p entropy on first 3 tokens of generation, threshold tuned on dev set. low compute overhead (tiny sample). config snippet: 
```json
{"gate": "entropy_first_k","k":3,"threshold": 2.4}
```

Ben: interesting. could the entropy threshold be brittle across prompts and quantization noise? quantized logits are noisier -> entropy estimation shifts. might need per-layer or per-prefix calibration.

Sophia: exactly. we should run calibration sweep: vary threshold from 1.6 -> 3.2 and measure false-negative (should have run exact but didn't) and false-positive rates. also compare k=1..5.

Elaine: on quant side: using q4_k_m with outlier clipping enabled. removing clipping moves the accuracy down another ~0.8 pts. so clipping helps. Dmitri, do we have kernel support for faster approx branches?

Dmitri: runtime can early-abort KV cache assembly for approx paths — small infra change. But need to ensure traceability for audits (can't silently change path for Private customers). infra-bot: this workspace enforces canary rollout. to deploy runtime change you must attach a canary config: 5% traffic for 24h, auto-rollback on >=2 regressions in 1h.

Sophia: For eval metrics, I recommend:
- n=2000 aggregated benchmark set (stratified by length)
- delta-accuracy and absolute accuracy
- regression-rate where gold->wrong (and severity tag: minor vs catastrophic)
- token-divergence (e.g., normalized edit distance)
- latency P50/P95/P99
- cost per 1k tokens estimate

Ben: also add human-reviewed sample of the catastrophic regressions (random 100 flagged) to see if they’re tolerable.

Elaine: action items:
- Dmitri: add shadow exact-decode logging for 10% of approx traffic (metrics + token diff) — due EOD tomorrow.
- Sophia: prepare the 2k benchmark and sweep plan (thresholds k=1..5, t=1.6..3.2) — due Tue.
- Ben: run quant-clipping ablation and post numbers to thread.

Dmitri: will push a small runtime flag and the shadow logger. quick note: logging increases disk write by ~8% so we should cap retention to 48h for the shadow runs.

Elaine: thanks. one more thought — if we can get 1.5x without >0.5pt accuracy loss, that's probably an acceptable trade for many Hosted customers (with a feature flag). Private contracts might want opt-out.

Sophia: agreed. will include customer-tier gating in rollout notes.

Ben: lgtm. after the 2k run we can decide: tune gate, or fallback to a slower but safer heuristic (e.g., lexical prefix matching + entropy).

Elaine: cool. uploading quick logs to the shared drive: https://redwood-internal/drive/ember7b/approx-quickpass (please comment findings here). :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deploy canary policy reminder — attach canary.yaml when creating runtime PR.
